 Trump faces Carney's refusal to back down as Canada pushes back against U.S. trade demands and Africa's largest economy turns to China 
 Awogbemila Temitope 
 14 November 2026 08:44 PM 
 Escalating commercial tariffs and trade friction under U.S. President Donald Trump are driving international partners to restructure their global economic relationships. In response to trade pressure from Washington, Canada is taking a firm stand to protect its auto manufacturing sector, while South Africa is shifting its commercial focus toward China. 
 U.S. President Donald Trump and Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney [Image Credit: Sky News] 
 Rising U.S. tariffs under President Trump are prompting global partners to reassess economic ties.
 Canada is refusing any new U.S. trade deal unless it secures its domestic auto industry.
 A major Canadian budget aims to diversify the economy and support sectors affected by American tariffs.
 South Africa, losing U.S. trade preferences, is rapidly expanding its exports to China.

 Canada resists United States trade demands to protect its automotive industry 
 Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney declared that Ottawa will not sign any new trade agreement with Washington that fails to guarantee a sustainable domestic auto sector. 
 Canada withdrew from bilateral negotiations three months ago after last-minute demands from Washington threatened Canadian vehicle manufacturing . 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Following a lengthy discussion with President Trump, Carney emphasized in Manila, " This government will not settle for a deal with the United States that is not consistent with a viable Canadian auto sector ," as reported by CBC News. 
 Carney added that reaching a stable automotive trade agreement quickly is " absolutely in the interest of course of Canadian workers, Canadian auto sector, but very much the U.S. as well ". 
 Canadian Prime Minister Mark CarneyANDREJ IVANOV / AFP 
 Business Insider USA 
 To reduce its economic reliance on the American market , the Canadian government introduced a C$142.1 billion national budget titled " Masters of our Destiny". 
 Funded in part by domestic oil revenue, the package finances critical mineral mining, energy production, housing, and direct financial support for auto and steel workers impacted by U.S. tariffs. 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 As reported by Business Insider Africa , Canadian Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne, said: " At its core, our plan is about changing Canada's growth model ". 
 Champagne emphasized that " no matter what happens south of the border, no matter what happens in the world, we will be more resilient, we will be stronger, we will be more independent ". 
 South Africa turns to China as trade policies in the U.S. shift 
 While Ottawa builds domestic self-reliance, South Africa is broadening its commercial partnerships across Asian markets following the loss of duty-free trade access to the American market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act. 
 Supported by a zero-tariff policy implemented by Beijing for qualifying African exports, South African shipments to China surged by nearly 25% between May and August 2026, while imports from China rose by 23%. 
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 This trade surge has expanded international markets for South African agricultural products , minerals, and manufactured goods. 
 Announcing the metrics in Pretoria, Chinese Ambassador Wu Peng expressed confidence that " more high-value-added South African products would enter the Chinese market in the future ". 
 Together, the actions taken by Ottawa and Pretoria reflect a broader shift as nations act to shield their economies from changing Washington trade policies.
